sales_evidence.proven_price_band: Volume sits at $40-80 (11,600+/mo, URPOWER-led) and, for premium, at $130+ where Ruff Liners sells 5,300+/mo on Amazon and RuffRover runs a $169.95 DTC kit with long-running Meta ads. Our price: $149 kit, inside the proven $130+ band and $21 under both leaders. Economics fail at $129 (see econ_results.sensitivity).

kit.hero_spec: Rigid back-seat extender in two sizes (Standard: cars and mid SUVs, about 52 x 25 in platform; XL: crew-cab trucks and full-size SUVs, about 58-60 x 28 in). Premium vs $40-66 Amazon versions, measurable: (1) 3-panel rigid board (honeycomb PP or aluminium-edged), not 6-8 small squares; spec a centre-point sag test, e.g. under 10 mm at 150 lb (ASSUMED target, verify on sample) because 8% of $50-100 reviews cite sag (4Knines analysis); (2) folds to a carton no longer than 20 in and under 1,728 cu in so it ships at actual weight (USPS) instead of dim weight; (3) quilted 600D or PU top, waterproof membrane, non-slip back, metal-tongue buckles and YKK zips (11% of $50-100 reviews cite strap/zip failures); (4) LATCH-compatible seat-belt and child-seat openings; (5) dye/heavy-metal-free fabric claim only with a test report (CPSIA not required: not a children's product). Weight claims in the category (400-600 lb static) are marketing; publish our own tested number. No electricals, so no UL/FCC.

ip.status: Active; filed Jun 7 2023, granted Feb 11 2025, expected expiry Aug 30 2043
ip.covers: One independent claim: a seat/cargo cover with middle, front and rear panels, each of heat-pressed layers; seat-belt openings; left and right door panels attached to the upper sides of the front panel; front and rear straps; AND left/right window inserts that slide into the window opening, each an L-shaped angle piece with an attachment strip in a recess. Ruff Liners cites it on the $169.99 extender for its door protection.
ip.avoidable: Yes. Every claim needs the window inserts (angle piece + attachment strip) and door panels attached to the front panel. A design must avoid: (1) any insert pushed into the window opening/seal, (2) door panels sewn or fastened to the extender's front panel. Strap-hung standalone door guards, or no door guards, avoid it. The $40-95 hard-bottom extenders avoid it because their door coverage is side flaps on the platform or none, with no window inserts.

ip.covers: Broader claim 1: same cover with door panels and removable window inserts having a leg that sits between the window glass and the interior window molding; method claims for the same.
ip.avoidable: Yes on the same basis: no window inserts, no door panels attached to the front panel. Watch for issuance.

ip.covers: Covers for fold-up truck rear seats. Claim 1 requires window inserts; claim 14 does NOT: front/middle/rear areas, rear area with independently foldable sections joined by a zipper, split-seat top clips either side of the zipper, top-seat straps, and door panels attached to the front area.
ip.avoidable: Yes. Our XL truck version must not combine zipped fold-up rear sections with clips AND door panels attached to the front. A rigid platform with headrest straps and no attached door panels avoids it.

ip.status: Active, granted Sep 9 2025, expiry about Apr 21 2043
ip.covers: Vehicle door guard whose bottom fastening strip secures to the underside of a seat cover, held vertical by fasteners, with a top elongated bar (also as a system with the seat cover).
ip.avoidable: Yes: door guards not fastened to the extender and without a top stiffening bar.

ip.covers: Claim 1 as filed is very broad (door-panel cover + coupling system attaching it to the car door interior); dependents add window clip with shim.
ip.avoidable: Probably (prior-art door protectors such as K&H have sold for years, so claim 1 is unlikely to issue as filed), but this is the main open item for any door guard: re-check before ordering; dropping door guards from the kit removes the risk.

ip.covers: U-shaped floor cover with an air-permeable vent port near the front-seat base.
ip.avoidable: Yes: no vent port in the front panel.

ip.covers: Pet hammock between front and rear seats with a front panel window screen integrally extended from a lower portion and specific hangers.
ip.avoidable: Yes if the mesh window is not integrally formed this way; mesh windows are common, so have the factory confirm their design is cleared.

ip.number: Design patents on back-seat extenders: USD1005742 S1 (Wei Li, 2023), USD1064669 S1 (Shenzhen Ligao, 2025), USD1046315 S1 (Zhilang Lin, 2024), USD1075161 S1 (Lifu Xu, 2025), USD1057302 S1 (Hongbin Zheng, 2025), USD1097354 S1 (EliteField, 2025), USD1141225 S1 (Jolly Innovation, 2026)
ip.covers: Ornamental appearance of specific extenders/seat covers.
ip.avoidable: Yes with a distinct appearance, but a factory's stock design may be one of these; compare the sample to each patent's figures before listing. These owners can file Amazon APEX complaints; less relevant off Amazon but still infringement.

ip.owner: Kevin Thompson US 7,677,662 (expired, fee); Gonzalez US 2015/0342340 (abandoned) on foam riding platforms
ip.covers: Hammock seat cover; foam platforms that fill the footwell
ip.avoidable: n/a (freedom-to-operate support for the basic footwell-platform idea)

ip.status: Shaodong TongxinDream v. Himmel, S.D. Tex. 4:25-cv-00846, filed Feb 26 2025 after Himmel filed an Amazon APEX complaint; voluntarily dismissed without prejudice (search snippets; docket not read)
ip.covers: Shows Ruff Liners enforces on Amazon
ip.avoidable: Avoid window inserts entirely. Not legal advice: a patent attorney should do a proper FTO before production.

fit.customer: Owners of medium to large dogs (often 2 dogs or an older dog) who drive them weekly in a mid-size SUV, crew-cab truck or sedan, are tired of the dog sliding into the footwell and of fur and scratches on seats and doors, and will pay $150-190 for something that looks finished and fits their exact car. Many are truck/SUV owners who have already bought a $40 hammock that sagged.
fit.positioning: Against Ruff Liners ($169.99, Shark Tank, window-insert door panels): 'Fits your exact car, or we tell you before you buy.' A rigid 3-panel platform with a published sag test, door guards that never touch the window seal or tint, and a kit priced $21 lower. Against URPOWER ($40-66): the same idea built not to sag, with a fit guarantee and premium materials.
fit.software_edge: (1) Year/make/model fit finder: Standard vs XL, seat type (bench, 60/40, captain's chairs = no), rear-door type, plus a 2-measurement check (front seatback to rear cushion edge at your driving position; door-to-door width), giving a fit verdict and a photo of the install in that body style. Fit data from customer measurements and published interior specs (to be compiled; UNKNOWN today). Ruff Liners already has a simple size selector and RuffRover asks customers to email, so ours must be clearly better. (2) Post-purchase install video by vehicle. (3) Order forwarding and delay notices for the 3PL, profit dashboard. Expected effect: fewer fit returns (refund ASSUMED 12% without, 5% with; no data).
fit.reorder: Weak. Mostly a one-time purchase. Paths: second-vehicle set, replacement washable topper/bed for the platform (RuffRover's free bed shows demand), front-seat cover, cargo liner for the same car, travel bowls and tethers. Products 2-3 should be a fitted cargo liner and a platform bed topper.
fit.seasonality: Google 'back seat extender for dogs' runs 880-1,600/mo: January 1,000 vs a 12-month average about 1,200 and a Jul-Aug peak of 1,600. 'dog car seat cover' January 9,900 vs 12,100 typical, 14,800 peaks (Mar, Nov). A Jan 4 test runs in a soft but not dead month; Amazon bought-past-month figures were taken in November and may be inflated by gifting.
risks: Cash: the item cannot be dropshipped from a US warehouse at a known price; a 15-25 kit batch landed costs about $900-1,500, well above the $300 working-capital line.
Shipping: if the board doesn't fold to <=20 in and <=1,728 cu in, shipping rises to $23-29 per order.
Fit returns on a bulky 9 lb item, with return shipping we may pay.
Competition: RuffRover already sells the same 'extender + free extras' kit DTC at $169.95 with 3,700+ reviews and 400+ day ads; Ruff Liners has Shark Tank and a patent.
IP: window-insert door panels (Himmel) and 4Knines door-guard patents; stock factory designs may copy a Chinese design patent.
Tariffs: classification and List 3 vs 4A uncertain; 20-45% of FOB.
Timeline: sampling plus sea freight before Jan 4 is tight; air freight hurts margin.

proposed_pts.demand_note: 32,000+ hard-bottom units/mo on Amazon (floor); 5,500+/mo at $130+; RuffRover DTC 3,700+ reviews with 400+ day Meta ads; 1,300 Google searches/mo for the exact term.
proposed_pts.supplier_note: Many audited factories at $8-15 basic, but no US-warehouse dropship price, premium spec unquoted, and a small batch costs 3-5x the working-capital line.
proposed_pts.differentiation_note: Fit finder and a tested no-sag board are real but copyable; RuffRover already sells the kit concept and Ruff Liners owns the 'door protection' story.
proposed_pts.risk_note: Patents are avoidable by design (no window inserts, no fastened door guards), no regulation; bulky shipping, fit returns and tariff uncertainty remain.
proposed_pts.ad_note: Very visual (dog sprawled instead of in the footwell, before/after); category proven on Meta by RuffRover's long-running ads; UGC with a real dog is easy.

top_unknowns: A supplier that ships single orders from US stock under our brand, or Dhruv's willingness to fund 15-25 kits of inventory (about $900-1,500 landed) beyond the $300 line
